| **Desk Rejection Rate** | No single source cleanly isolates a pure desk-reject-only percentage. APA Journal Survey Project: of 468 logged initial verdicts, 81.62% were rejected at the initial-verdict stage (mixes desk rejects and post-review rejects), 17.09% got revise-and-resubmit, 0.21% accepted outright. Daily Nous commenters separately describe desk rejects specifically as 'very few' with most submissions going to referees and getting a verdict with comments within ~3 months. AAP's own journal page states ~750 submissions/year yield ~60 published articles+discussion notes/year (~8% output ratio, not a true acceptance-rate figure since publication counts lag intake year). | WO2 |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | AAP/journal-specific submission guidance (fetched from aap.org.au/submissions, 2026-07-13): authors must acknowledge and document any significant use of generative AI tools beyond grammar correction or prose refinement. Implication: minor language-polishing use is unrestricted/undisclosed; substantive use (drafting content, argument generation) requires disclosure. This is journal/AAP-specific, distinct from but consistent with publisher Taylor & Francis's general AI policy. T&F's own policy page (taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so publisher-level detail is relayed only via third-party WebSearch snippets, not verbatim-read: generative AI tools may not be listed as authors, and any use must be disclosed per T&F's general author guidance. |
| **Source URL** | https://aap.org.au/submissions |

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** Analytic-tradition philosophy across all areas and its history; the journal explicitly states it is not narrow despite its analytic reputation. No 2025-2026 special issue or CFP was found via direct search - appears to run as a standard general-submission journal with no current thematic call. Journal closes to new submissions each Australasian summer (2025-26 window: closed Dec 1, reopened mid-February).

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** articles (unsolicited), discussion notes (unsolicited), book reviews (solicited only)

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Daily Nous 2024 crowd-sourced thread (English-language, first-hand author reports): editor praised for exceptional responsiveness and fairness, e.g. giving 'balanced and fair explanations... even when it's a reject,' and mediating between referees with divergent views by including 'advice on how to steer between them' in the decision letter. Historic editor Stephen Hetherington was singled out by name for responsiveness in a 2015 Daily Nous thread; current editor per AAP is Antony Eagle (Adelaide), since 2022 - the 2024 praise may reflect either editor's tenure and is not attributed to a named individual in that thread. AAP's own referee guidance instructs reviewers to judge papers on quality of argumentation rather than agreement with the paper's conclusions. No Chinese-language (小木虫/知乎/fabiaoji) or Reddit r/AskAcademia discussion of this journal was found.

- **ai_policy (verbatim publisher-level detail)**: taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; publisher-level claims are relayed only via WebSearch AI-summary snippets of that page (not a first-hand read), so confidence is capped. The journal-specific AAP statement (fetched directly) is the higher-confidence source and is reported as the primary fact.
- **positioning.accepts_now (current CFP / recent article sample)**: Direct WebSearch for a 2025-2026 special issue/CFP returned no results, and tandfonline current-issue table of contents (rajp20/toc) could not be fetched (403), so recent article titles were not independently enumerated. Positioning is inferred only from AAP's general aims-and-scope language, not from a sample of actual recent article titles/topics.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture (cross-language)**: No results found on 小木虫 (muchong.com), 知乎 (zhihu), fabiaoji, or Reddit for this journal (see cross_language_checked); the Chinese/general-forum academic community appears to have negligible discussion of this niche analytic-philosophy venue.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct (precise single figure)**: APA survey's 81.62% initial-rejection rate and Daily Nous's characterization of desk rejects as 'very few' measure different things (overall initial-verdict rejection vs. true no-review desk reject) and cannot be reconciled into one clean number from available sources.
